xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3894: Deacon patrol list is still 68 entries: delete the 30 pending repairers once counters prove them dead, then move the 38 housekeeping chores off the 60s patrol loop

plan.title: Deacon patrol list is still 68 entries: delete the 30 pending repairers once counters prove them dead, then move the 38 housekeeping chores off the 60s patrol loop
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5-1

narratives.Problem: After the substrate epic, runPatrol() still runs 68 budgeted patrols (plus 5 alarms) every 60 seconds: 30 state-repair patrols awaiting soak-gated deletion and 38 Keep/Rewire chores that ride the tick only because it was there. The tick should be stuck detection and pipeline progress; housekeeping belongs on slower, durable cadences. The deletions are gated on 7 clean days of would-fire counters, and on 2026-09-18 that evidence is one day old for 22 patrols, absent for 7 (no counter sites), and invalid for reconcileInFlightJournals (its counter records the F15 enriched-vs-raw delta: 145 firings in 5 hours).
narratives.Proposal: Part B now: a declarative patrol registry (src/lib/cloister/patrol-registry.ts: 14 TICK_PATROLS and 29 HOUSEKEEPING_CHORES with fast=5min/hourly/daily cadences), a housekeeping scheduler (src/lib/cloister/housekeeping-scheduler.ts) that ticks every 60s and runs a chore when now - lastRunAt >= cadence with lastRunAt persisted to ~/.overdeck/deacon/housekeeping.json (durable across pan reload, single-flight, pause-aware, budgeted through runBudgetedPatrol), runPatrol reduced to the 14 tick steps plus the 30 pending-soak steps, pan doctor printing a Patrol cadences table, and the no-loss audit holding TICK ∪ CHORES against Appendix C. Part A prerequisites now: would-fire counters and shadow gates for the six counter-less Phase 4 patrols, an honest reconcileInFlightJournals counter (real journal folds only), and deletion of the checkStuckWorkAgents no-op stub. Part A deletions (30 patrols, one commit each, family audit fixtures) are filed as PAN-3895 with the decision rule and per-patrol map, executable once each patrol has 7 clean days (earliest 2026-09-25).
narratives.NonGoals:
- Deleting any of the 29 remaining PENDING_SOAK_DELETION patrols in this issue (PAN-3895 owns them; their evidence windows are not open)
- Writing the family no-loss audit fixtures for those deletions (PAN-3895)
- A Docker events subscriber or any new reactive handler; existing reactive primaries in service-reactive.ts are unchanged and the polled runs become slower backstops
- Making cadences configurable via cloister config; the three classes are constants in the registry
- Changing the five exempt alarm patrols, the patrol budget mechanism, the invariant checker, the stall sweeper, or the 15s resource-pressure timer
- Changing shadow-mode semantics (OVERDECK_PATROL_SHADOW) or the would-fire file format
- Any dashboard UI for cadences (pan doctor is the only surface)
- Moving refreshHostHeartbeatForEphemeralVms off the tick (the VM watchdog kills machines after a 5-minute heartbeat gap)
- Touching model routing, effort, or spawn flags
- Manual triggering of housekeeping chores: POST /api/deacon/patrol runs the 60s tick only
- Chore actions in PatrolResult.actionsToken / GET /api/deacon/status (they reach GET /api/deacon/logs and the deacon log file through appendDeaconLog)

autoDecisions.summary: Split the 30 deletions into sibling PAN-3895; PAN-3894 delivers Part B plus the non-time-gated Part A prerequisites.
autoDecisions.rationale: Deletion evidence needs 7 clean days per patrol; on 2026-09-18 it is 1 day old for 22 patrols, absent for 7 (no recordWouldFire sites), and invalid for reconcileInFlightJournals (F15 noise). A single issue would hold an open deacon.ts PR for a week after Part B lands.

autoDecisions.summary: Tick set is 14 steps: 5 alarms, the invariant checker, swarm janitor, checkPostReviewCommits, patrolStrikeLandings, monitorReviewConvoySignals, checkDeadEndAgents, nudgeIdleWorkAgentsWithOpenBeads, checkThinkingSignatureCorruption, refreshHostHeartbeatForEphemeralVms.
autoDecisions.rationale: These are stuck recovery, tick-debounced (checkPostReviewCommits needs two consecutive ticks), 1-minute-windowed (checkMassDeath), or time-critical (EPHEMERAL_HEARTBEAT_STALE_THRESHOLD_SECONDS = 300 in remote-agents.ts would let the VM watchdog kill machines on a slower heartbeat).

autoDecisions.summary: Three cadence classes (fast 5 min, hourly, daily) with durable per-chore lastRunAt in ~/.overdeck/deacon/housekeeping.json, checked by a 60s scheduler tick.
autoDecisions.rationale: patrolCycle is persisted so today's % 60 gates survive pan reload; bare hourly/daily setIntervals would reset on every restart and daily chores would rarely fire on a machine that reloads several times a day. A staleness sweep of every moved chore found no internal grace or cooldown under 2 minutes, so 5-minute latency is safe.

autoDecisions.summary: No new event-driven infrastructure; existing reactive handlers stay primary and their polled runs move to hourly.
autoDecisions.rationale: reconcileClosedIssueAgents, reconcileOrphanProposedSpecs and reconcileIdleWorkspaceStacks already have reactive handlers in service-reactive.ts. Strike-workspace reaping cannot key on the merge event because the strike session is still alive when the merge lands. A Docker events stream is new surface with no proven need; container health polls at 5 minutes with its existing 60s backoff floor.

autoDecisions.summary: Container-restart backoff bookkeeping becomes process-local in-memory state instead of DeaconState.
autoDecisions.rationale: Off-tick, checkWorkspaceContainerHealth cannot share runPatrol's in-memory state and a separate saveState clobbers it (deacon.ts:2419 comment). Losing the map across a dashboard restart only grants a crash-looping container up to five more attempts per process.

autoDecisions.summary: Fix the reconcileInFlightJournals counter to fire only on a genuine journal fold instead of treating its nonzero count as a transition gap.
autoDecisions.rationale: Appendix C row #4 and epic W27 both document that the patrol compares an enriched read against the raw row and fires forever (F15). Its 145 firings in 5 hours are that noise; left alone it would also cross its 50/day budget daily and page the operator.

autoDecisions.summary: Delete checkStuckWorkAgents in this issue without a soak.
autoDecisions.rationale: The function body is `return []` (deacon.ts:814-816, "Retained as a no-op stub"); it repairs nothing, so a counter would be zero by construction and the audit evidence is the source itself.
Karpathy rule 2: no configurability that was not requested; the issue asks for a decision per chore, not a knob.

autoDecisions.summary: Deacon-resident chore functions are injected into the registry through a ChoreContext; the registry never references deacon.js; deacon.ts imports the scheduler statically.
autoDecisions.rationale: scripts/lint-circular-deps.sh runs madge, which counts dynamic imports as edges (verified with a two-file fixture on 2026-09-18). Reachability over the madge graph shows no chore module or scheduler dependency reaches deacon.ts or service.ts, so injection removes the only possible new cycle.

metadata.sizeJustification: The issue was already decomposed: the time-gated 30 deletions are PAN-3895. What remains has one shared mutation point (src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts, edited by five items in a serial chain) and one shared audit file; the file count (29) is dominated by two-line test and doc touches, and the subsystems are src/lib, src/cli, tests/unit, tests/lib, scripts, docs, CLAUDE.md. Splitting further would put the registry, the scheduler, and the runPatrol rewiring in separate PRs that each conflict on deacon.ts.
